Built between anchorages.\nShaped by the water outside our own hatch.
A free, practical anchor watch born from life aboard Yokuli.

Before turning his life towards the sea, kuku worked as a programmer. In New Zealand, sailing stopped being a distant idea and became part of everyday life.

Our small crew sails Yokuli, a Lotus 10.6 designed by New Zealand yacht designer Alan Wright. We have refitted her with our own hands — not to make her a showpiece, but to make her a capable home for the miles ahead.

We want to begin close to home: the islands scattered around New Zealand, the bays tucked behind its headlands, and the quiet anchorages that are easy to miss from land. If wind, time and life allow, we hope one day to point Yokuli farther out and see more of the world.

Anchor Watch grew naturally from that life. Kuku brought a programmer’s habit aboard: when a problem keeps returning, understand it, then build a tool that earns its place. A simple anchor alarm gradually became NMEA tools, anchor-centre estimation, personal depth mapping and the other things we actually wanted at sea.

Yoyo is our captain; kuku and lili complete the crew. We are still learning, and the water has a reliable way of correcting confident ideas. That is why the app keeps changing with real use aboard Yokuli — and why its complete feature set will remain free.
Follow Yokuli’s refit and our voyage from New Zealand’s islands and bays towards whatever lies beyond.
Anchor Watch’s complete feature set is free. If the project is useful to you, you can voluntarily support continued sailing, testing and development. Support does not unlock app features.

We build features when we actually find a reason for them aboard Yokuli. Some ideas survive real boat use. Some don’t. The useful ones make it into Anchor Watch.
Have an idea or a feature request? Send it directly to kuku. Requests are read carefully and we’ll try to help when practical, but no individual feature or delivery date can be promised.
Anchor Watch has no account, advertising or analytics. Anchor, track, NMEA diagnostics and sonar data stay on this device unless you deliberately export or share them.

Map sources: Google Maps; OpenSeaMap seamarks with OpenStreetMap attribution; New Zealand marine data from Land Information New Zealand (LINZ). Providers may require a network connection and have their own terms. Marine overlays are reference aids, never a substitute for official charts or a proper watch.
